description:
stoa-mail exposes a SCIM 2.0 endpoint for IdP push provisioning. Solves the cold-start problem: grants exist before the user's first login, not after.

Endpoint: /scim/v2/ — Users and Groups resources per RFC 7643/7644
Methods: POST, GET, PATCH, PUT, DELETE on /scim/v2/Users and /scim/v2/Groups
Discovery: GET /scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig

SCIM event → stoa action mapping:
  User created/updated (active=true): upsert identities, link identity_providers, auto-provision email-claim grants
  User active=false: set identities.active=FALSE, set explicit_deny=TRUE on all grants for this identity — immediate revocation regardless of token state
  Group member added: look up group_mailbox_grants, pre-provision mailbox_grants with source=scim-group
  Group member removed: revoke grants WHERE source=scim-group for this identity+group. Admin grants untouched.
  Group deleted: revoke all grants WHERE source=scim-group for this group

Security requirements:
  Separate long-lived bearer token from admin API token (different credential, different rotation schedule)
  Not publicly routable — restrict to IdP IP ranges or require mTLS
  Full audit log on every SCIM operation (who provisioned what when)
  Rate limiting

Config in mail.toml:
  [scim]
  enabled = true
  bearer_token = "secretx:aws-sm:prod/stoa/scim-token"
  allowed_cidrs = ["185.234.218.0/24"]  # IdP IP ranges

SCIM is only enabled for trust_level=managed providers. verified/federated providers do not get SCIM access.
title: design: SCIM 2.0 provisioning endpoint
